data.title: The data
data.lead: What the industry expert asked for: efficiency by hour and by station, the operation that holds the module back, and productive minutes.
eff.title: Module efficiency by hour
eff.lead_html: How much of the paid time turned into standard minutes of T-shirt (<button type="button" class="tip" data-tip="sam">SAM</button>, <button type="button" class="tip" data-tip="eficiencia">efficiency</button>). Hours covered by the camera open on video.

gl.title: How to read this data
gl.p1: We talk about stations and the module, not about people. No names, and no rankings of people.
gl.p2: It is meant to balance the work and support the team: we keep sewing time apart from waiting and walking time.
gl.p3: Every number says where it comes from (video, CP or example) and how sure we are.
gl.p4: All times are plant time. The clock inside the video runs one hour ahead.
tip.sam.d: Standard minutes the garment should take at a normal pace. The {product} T-shirt has {sam} min in CP.
tip.eficiencia.d: Standard minutes produced ÷ minutes people had available. {p} means working right at standard.
tip.takt.d: How often a piece has to come off the line to hit the target. For {target} pieces per hour: 3600 s ÷ {target} = {takt} s.
tip.ciclo.d: The time Station B spends on one piece: going for it, coming back, sewing it and handing it off.
tip.cola.d: Pieces Station A leaves on its table, ready for Station B.
tip.registro.d: Each time a piece is keyed in on the EnPiso CP keypad.
tip.restriccion.d: The operation or station that is slowest against its standard: the one that sets the pace for the whole module.
tip.confianza.d: High: checked one by one. Medium: measured on video, within a few seconds. Low: the camera only sees it part of the time.
proof.cap: Proof on video. Tap a picture to open that moment.
